chapter_title_en: The Broken Horn World’s First Contact
chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch. 466 – First Contact with the Broken Horn World
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning finally encounters life in the Realm of Annihilation. The warrior civilization of the Broken Horn World tests his strength, leading to a quick skirmish and a chillingly pragmatic retreat.
og_title: First Contact in the Void: The Broken Horn World Tests Ji Ning
og_description: Ji Ning's first encounter with a living civilization in the void is tense, deadly, and ends with a cold, calculated retreat from the Broken Horn World's commander.
twitter_title: The Broken Horn World’s first contact with Ji Ning is a mess of whips and decapitations.
twitter_description: Ji Ning meets the first locals in the Realm of Annihilation. The Broken Horn World sends soldiers to test him. They fail.

lore_anchors.definition: The eternally dark, storm-ravaged void between the Three Realms and the broader Chaosverse. It is featureless, devoid of Dao resonance, and forces cultivators to rely solely on physical arts and Heartforce for survival.
A terrifying, broken super-continent that lingers in the void. It is so dangerous that even True Gods and Daofathers dare not trespass within it carelessly.

The territory of a powerful alien civilization in the void. Its warriors are massive, scaled beings with golden or red eyes and curved horns, who treat the surrounding void as their sovereign territory.
The ancient, universal language of the primordial Fiendgods. Any being with sufficient intelligence can understand it innately upon hearing it.
A movement technique that allows Ji Ning to use his divine power for incredibly fast, aggressive movement, even in environments where he cannot borrow the power of Heaven and Earth.
A top-ten divine ability since Pangu, created by Daoist Threelives; allows the cultivator to use their hands as ultimate weapons, shattering defenses that would resist flying swords and divine sense.

The supreme divine ability beneath the True God level, trained by mastering nine cycles of body refinement; provides a powerful, passive defensive layer that makes the user extremely difficult to harm.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn't Ji Ning use the Starseizing Hand?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He didn't need to. He appraised the enemy's strength as lower than his base power, so he chose to conserve his trump card and only used his swordsmanship to dispatch them.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Broken Horn World commander retreat?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He performed a cost-benefit analysis. Ji Ning's performance (Sky-class speed/technique) suggested he was an elite scout, not a pushover. Losing his soldiers, which he views as replaceable breeding stock, was not worth the risk of over-committing.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Can Ji Ning fly faster than the ships here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not necessarily. The void ship was described as moving at an astonishing speed, and it was entirely hidden. Ji Ning's advantage is his close-quarters combat speed and technique, not his raw travel speed in this hostile environment.
